correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the pivot/first-neighbor matching in RESULT.md lines 14–18. For a downward unmatched step at a node, removal of the branch-defining neighbor can only move to a later branch or the toggle class; matched arrows preserve that class. Inside the toggle class, up adds the pivot and an unmatched down cannot delete it, so no directed cycle exists. Induct inside each branch. Removing the empty-face pair gives exactly one critical vertex without changing the 8/9 boundary. Independent replay `python3 /workspace/review_evidence/grid9_replay.py <frozen verification/certificate.json>` recovered the 182 and 19 critical masks, all 159 signed entries (max absolute value 2), and the +1 determinant by rational elimination, without executing the submitted verifier. The replay also confirmed all face counts by closed-neighborhood deletion (7,594,361 total including empty; reduced Euler characteristic 163). The Morse reduction sums signed alternating paths with the negative inverse incidence for each up step; paths starting at an upper-paired eight-face cannot reach a critical eight-face. The resulting CW model is simply connected with reduced homology only in degree 8, free of rank 163 by the primitive full-column-rank minor. Hurewicz supplies maps representing a basis and the homological Whitehead theorem makes their wedge a homotopy equivalence. This verifies an integral homotopy classification, not merely agreement of Betti numbers.

originality.rationale: Chauhan–Sharma–Shukla, arXiv:2609.27366v1 (2026-09-23), §4 Table 1 explicitly reports the integral homology group Z^163 in degree 8 at width 9, and the immediately following paragraph explicitly concludes a wedge of (n−1)-spheres for 3≤n≤9 using simple connectivity. Together these give the exact 163-eight-sphere homotopy type for the same strip before the frozen finding. The frozen self-review lacked the full text and incorrectly treats this as an outstanding case. The current Morse certificate is an independently reproducible route, not a new stated homotopy classification.
